scope.purpose: Independent small connector sample: typed async capability face, optional script slot, distinguishable refusal/failure outcomes and delegation-only infrastructure.

origins.note: App-port with @ImplementedBy(infrastructure impl) analogy only; not a connector algorithm source.
Byte-identical frozen copy of the approved first-family values; nominal vocabulary reused, never re-edited here.

origins.description: This input explicitly defines the sample connector, protocol, results and delegation contract. Not historical truth, not approved production business semantics.

legalDomain.identifiers: WarehouseId, SkuId and LocationId reuse the frozen first-family nominal domain: ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._-], length 1..64; illegal texts fail decoding, never coerce.
legalDomain.probeProtocol: Exactly one line, no LF or CR. ANSWER|<sku>|<nonnegative Long> or REFUSED|<code>|<message>. Exact three-field arity; separator characters are structurally excluded by the arity check.
legalDomain.refusalFields: code and message are nonempty; a refusal is a typed business result on the success channel, never a failure-channel conversion.
legalDomain.directoryProtocol: Exactly one line, no LF or CR. DIRECTORY|<warehouseId>|<loc1>,<loc2,...>; an empty tail decodes to the empty vector; a trailing location separator is malformed; repeated locations stay verbatim in declared order.
legalDomain.failureChannels: Transport failures and ProtocolViolation values live on the Future failure channel; refusals and answers live on the success channel. No shape is ever synthesized from a failure.
legalDomain.runner: NodeSubprocessRunner.run performs exactly one subprocess execution per call; no retry, no timeout semantics declared in this sample.
legalDomain.dependency: The implementation delegates only: one runner call per port call, verbatim script, typed lifting. ExecutionContext is injected explicitly and used only for Future transformation.

protocolViolation.name: ProtocolViolation
protocolViolation.note: Constructed as a value and placed on the failure channel; never thrown, never converted into a business result.

runner.name: NodeSubprocessRunner
runner.contract: def run(script: String): Future[String] yielding one output line
runner.role: handwritten injection seam; concrete subprocess mechanics belong to connector-implementation

delegationGuarantees: exactly one runner call per port call

decisions.choice: Keep the traditional @ImplementedBy(classOf[infrastructure Impl]) annotation with its application-to-infrastructure import, matching the curated CreditBalanceRepository analogy; bootstrap-binding alternative not taken.
The sample implementation matches the port ABI exactly: both methods, both parameter shapes, shared typed lifting; the impl-family debt of first-method-only/parameters-Nil is not reproduced.

Drop the unused javax.inject._ wildcard, import scala.concurrent.Future as a short name, and use a single alphabetically sorted import block per file; recorded as an explicit formatting exception against the raw template.
Malformed payloads, illegal identifiers and non-single-line inputs always fail with a named ProtocolViolation on the failure channel; nothing is silently defaulted, truncated or coerced.
This sample migrates the traditional Node-tool connector capability face only; formal typed TechnicalPorts mapping stays out of scope.
